statements.status_notes: PostgreSQL fixed CVE-2026-120145 (PostgreSQL logical replication can write to subscriber system catalogs, executing arbitrary code) in 16.16 on the PostgreSQL 16 branch: https://www.postgresql.org/support/security/CVE-2026-120145/ lists 16.16 as the fixed release for major version 16, and the 16.16 release notes, https://www.postgresql.org/docs/release/16.16/, list this CVE. The fix is commit https://github.com/postgres/postgres/commit/71bb0b5877e4bbd43ac0bafbd4f9d360ea7dedf7 on the REL_16_STABLE branch, which changes src/backend/commands/subscriptioncmds.c, src/backend/executor/execReplication.c, src/backend/replication/logical/relation.c, src/backend/replication/logical/worker.c and src/include/executor/executor.h so that the subscriber itself refuses a system catalog or temporary relation as a logical replication target, instead of relying on the publisher not to name one; it is tagged Security: CVE-2026-120145 and is in the REL_16_16 release tag and not in REL_16_15. The advisory states that only subscriptions owned by a superuser are vulnerable. The DHI postgresql16 packages for Alpine 3.23 are built from Alpine's postgresql16 APKBUILD, https://github.com/alpinelinux/aports/blob/859fa0795e895af033fab32094a83301f2b4d8ff/community/postgresql16/APKBUILD, which builds the upstream PostgreSQL release tarball; none of the patches it applies touch the files this fix changes. We checked the postgres server binary, /usr/libexec/postgresql16/postgres, in every published postgresql16 package for Alpine 3.23 on both x86_64 and aarch64 (checksums verified against the package index): 16.16-r0 reports PostgreSQL 16.16 and carries the fix, while the earlier builds 16.13-r0, 16.14-r0 and 16.15-r0 report 16.13, 16.14 and 16.15 and are affected. This fix adds no distinctive message string, so the per-build evidence is the version each server binary reports. 16.16-r0 is the first published build that carries the fix. Alpine's postgresql16 APKBUILD lists CVE-2026-120145 under its 16.16-r0 secfixes.

PostgreSQL fixed CVE-2026-120145 (PostgreSQL logical replication can write to subscriber system catalogs, executing arbitrary code) in 18.7 for major version 18: https://www.postgresql.org/support/security/CVE-2026-120145/ lists 18.7 as the fixed release for 18, and the 18.7 release notes, https://www.postgresql.org/docs/release/18.7/, list this CVE. The fix is commit https://github.com/postgres/postgres/commit/cc2d1a4c981bd83f2ba54c540c9e2bb9832dbb18 on the REL_18_STABLE branch, tagged Security: CVE-2026-120145 and Backpatch-through: 14, in the REL_18_7 release tag and not in REL_18_6. It changes src/backend/commands/subscriptioncmds.c, src/backend/executor/execReplication.c, src/backend/replication/logical/relation.c, src/backend/replication/logical/worker.c and src/include/executor/executor.h so that the subscriber itself refuses to use a system catalog or a temporary relation as a logical replication target. The DHI postgresql18 packages for Alpine 3.23 are built from Alpine's postgresql18 APKBUILD, https://github.com/alpinelinux/aports/blob/59a1f1d230675807d5a95a0c1e57ba5d640ba039/main/postgresql18/APKBUILD, which builds the upstream PostgreSQL release tarball; none of the patches it applies touch the files this fix changes, and it lists CVE-2026-120145 under its 18.7-r0 secfixes. The DHI Alpine 3.23 package repository (x86_64 and aarch64) publishes packages built from source postgresql18 at 18.1-r0, 18.2-r0, 18.3-r0, 18.4-r0, 18.6-r0 and 18.7-r0. The vulnerable code is in the postgres server binary, /usr/libexec/postgresql18/postgres, which the postgresql18 package ships in every one of those builds on both architectures. We checked every published postgresql18 package for Alpine 3.23 on both x86_64 and aarch64 (checksums verified against the package index): the postgres server binary in 18.7-r0 reports PostgreSQL 18.7, while the earlier builds 18.1-r0, 18.2-r0, 18.3-r0, 18.4-r0 and 18.6-r0 report 18.1, 18.2, 18.3, 18.4 and 18.6. The error messages the fix uses also appear in the server binary of earlier builds, so the boundary rests on the release version that the server binary of each build reports. The earlier builds are upstream releases before 18.7, so they are affected; 18.7-r0 is the first published build that carries the fix.

PostgreSQL fixed CVE-2026-120145, a missing authorization check in logical replication that lets a compromised publisher write to system catalogs of a superuser-owned subscription and execute arbitrary code, in 17.12 (https://www.postgresql.org/support/security/CVE-2026-120145/, https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-120145, https://www.postgresql.org/docs/release/17.12/). Earlier 17 releases are affected. The server binary in this owner's 17.12-0 build and in its rebuild of Debian's 17.12-0+deb13u1 reports PostgreSQL 17.12 on amd64 and arm64, so both carry the fix. The 17.11-1 build and the current rebuild of Debian's 17.11-0+deb13u1 report PostgreSQL 17.11, and the earlier rebuilds of Debian's 17.10-0+deb13u1 and 17.11-0+deb13u1, no longer in the repository, package PostgreSQL 17.10 and 17.11. All of these are affected and sort below 17.12-0.

PostgreSQL fixed CVE-2026-120145, a missing authorization check in logical replication that lets a compromised publisher write to system catalogs of a superuser-owned subscription and execute arbitrary code, in 17.12 (https://www.postgresql.org/support/security/CVE-2026-120145/, https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-120145, https://www.postgresql.org/docs/release/17.12/). Earlier 17 releases are affected. The server binary in this owner's 17.12-0 build and in its rebuild of Debian's 17.12-0+deb13u1 reports PostgreSQL 17.12 on amd64 and arm64, so both carry the fix. The 17.11-1 build and the current rebuild of Debian's 17.11-0+deb13u1 report PostgreSQL 17.11, and the earlier rebuilds of Debian's 17.10-0+deb13u1 and 17.11-0+deb13u1, no longer in the repository, package PostgreSQL 17.10 and 17.11. All of these are affected and sort below 17.12-0.
